title: Achraf Kassioui Keyboard - Romantic Skeuomorphism of Mechanical Input

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A mechanical keyboard (Filco Majestouch TKL, red Esc, purple WASD): keycaps wobble slightly on their switches, depress under force, and cast moving shadows as they actuate.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: The onscreen keyboard mirrors the physical one bidirectionally: keys wobble on hover, depress on mousedown, AND depress when the user types on their own physical keyboard; Caps/Scroll Lock indicators sync with real hardware state. Clicking keys types into a text area; hold-and-drag gives a piano glissando.

design_tokens.borders: Keycap silhouettes with 3D top faces and side walls; legends engraved-style
design_tokens.elevation: Per-key cast shadows that deepen on actuation - the shadow IS the key travel indicator
design_tokens.typography: Compact keycap legends in two stacked rows (symbol + fn label) like real doubleshot caps

interactive_mechanics: Two-way key state sync: onscreen keys depress from real keyboard input
Hardware indicator LEDs (Caps/Scroll Lock) reflect the user's actual device
Hover wobble, mousedown depress, hold-drag piano effect
Keyboard-shortcut display mode reusing the same key objects
usability_notes: The decisive pattern is bidirectional sync - the skeuomorph responds to the user's REAL device, which makes the metaphor feel alive rather than decorative. Best as a settings/shortcut surface or a delight moment. Weaknesses are documented by the author honestly: heavy image assets, poor touch optimization, limited functionality - a desktop-first experiment. Accessibility: keys must remain real buttons; visual travel is decoration only. Author's own 2017 experiment page, self-documented.
